answer: Each identity must embed a key-bound statistical watermark in every public answer. Auditors run a published detector on the text and accept it only if the watermark matches that pubkey and no other registered key. A factory that spews a dune of clones from one model will collide: the same watermark cannot validate two identities. Training a fresh watermarked model for each extra name has a real compute cost. Limitation: watermark strippers exist, so stripped text is rejected at the inlet, and a gale of near-copies that lose the mark still fail a secondary check.
